}

  }

}

rawInput.answer: Errors propagate on two levels: inside compose.ts's per-frame `try { res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1)) } catch(err)` — if `err instanceof Error` and an `onError` (the app's `errorHandler`, settable via `app.onError()`) was passed to `compose()`, it's handled right there (`onError(err, context)`, `context.error = err`, response set) so the throw never reaches outer middleware, which resume normally after their `await next()`; otherwise it rethrows and bubbles up through the chain of awaited `next()` calls. At the top, `hono-base.ts#dispatch()` wraps the whole `composed(c)` call (or the single-handler fast path) in its own try/catch calling `#handleError`, which invokes `this.errorHandler` for `Error` instances (default handler special-cases `HTTPException`-like objects with `getResponse()`, else logs and returns 500) or rethrows non-Error values uncaught.

rawInput.answer: Middleware composition is implemented in src/compose.ts via the `compose()` function (based on koa-compose), which builds a `dispatch(i)` recursive/async chain over an array of `[handler, next]` middleware tuples, handling errors via `onError` and 404s via `onNotFound`. It's invoked from src/hono-base.ts — in `Hono#route()`/mounting logic (line ~226) and in the request dispatch method `#dispatch`/`fetch` path (line ~451, `compose(matchResult[0], this.errorHandler, this.#notFoundHandler)`) where matched route handlers are composed into a single callable chain.

compose imported at line 7; used at line 226 (route mounting) and line 451 (main request dispatch)

relevantFiles.reason: Core implementation of middleware composition (the compose function)
Consumes compose() to build the request handling pipeline and for sub-app mounting

uncertainty: Did not inspect router.ts internals for how matchResult[0] (the middleware array) is constructed, only confirmed compose() consumes it.

verified.summary: compose() in src/compose.ts implements middleware chaining via recursive dispatch(i), calling handler(context, ()=>dispatch(i+1)), catching errors for onError, and invoking onNotFound when no handler matches.

report.answer: Errors propagate on two levels: inside compose.ts's per-frame `try { res = await handler(context, () => dispatch(i+1)) } catch(err)` — if `err instanceof Error` and an `onError` (the app's `errorHandler`, settable via `app.onError()`) was passed to `compose()`, it's handled right there (`onError(err, context)`, `context.error = err`, response set) so the throw never reaches outer middleware, which resume normally after their `await next()`; otherwise it rethrows and bubbles up through the chain of awaited `next()` calls. At the top, `hono-base.ts#dispatch()` wraps the whole `composed(c)` call (or the single-handler fast path) in its own try/catch calling `#handleError`, which invokes `this.errorHandler` for `Error` instances (default handler special-cases `HTTPException`-like objects with `getResponse()`, else logs and returns 500) or rethrows non-Error values uncaught.

verified.summary: compose()'s dispatch(i) wraps each handler call in try/catch; Error instances go to onError (sets context.error, context.res, isError=true) inline at the frame where they occurred, non-Error or missing-onError cases rethrow up the awaited next() chain.
verified.evidence: src/compose.ts full contents (read in turn 1, reused per ledger)

verified.summary: Default errorHandler checks 'getResponse' in err (HTTPException-style) to build a Response, otherwise console.error + generic 500 text response; app.onError() overrides this.errorHandler which flows into compose() as onError.

At the top, `hono-base.ts#dispatch()` wraps the whole `composed(c)` call (or the single-handler fast path) in its own try/catch calling `#handleError`, which invokes `this.errorHandler` for `Error` instances (default handler special-cases `HTTPException`-like objects with `getResponse()`, else logs and returns 500) or rethrows non-Error values uncaught.
